page.layout: One page of text, with marginal notes in the left margin. Running head at the top. No page number visible. Left margin: three notes (an Arabic note at the top, a note on Polus and Scaliger, and an Arabic note with its translation). Main text in one column.

main_text.p: {*} ad tempora sua perduxisse testatur. Floruit ergo quo tempore Tatari Moguli Mesopotamiam & Syriam pervaserunt, quorum res gestas tradit à Ingiscban ( qui occiso Vng-Chan, eo qui ﻟﻲ ﺯﻣﺎﺩﻭﺣﻧﺎ ﻣﻠﻚ Rex Iuhanna, seu Iohannes, dictus est, è tribu ﻛﺮﻳﺖ Carrit, quae Christianam professa est religionem, ad imperium evectus est circa annum Alex. 1514. Hejrae 599.) usque ad Abaga Il-Chan, anno Hejrae 675. ( quo tempore obiit Nasiroddinus Tusiensis, Philosophus & Mathematicus insignis,) vel, ut in altero exemplari, usque ad Argun Il-Chan; anno Hejrae 683, Alex. 1596.

Historiam autem suam, quam in decem {*} Dy-nastias divisit, contexuisse se scribit ex eorum qui hoc in genere diversis linguis, Sy-riacâ scil. Arabica, aliisque scripserunt, monumentis. In priore ejus parte, secutum se ait, Eusebium,& Andronicum Chronologos, quòd cum iis convenisse videret, eruditissimo Viro Iacobo Robawien.si, trium linguarum Hebrai-cae scil. Graecae & Syriacae peritiâ insigni. In eâ quae Arabes & Mohammedanos spectat, secutus praecipuè videtur Saedum quendam, Ebn Ahmed

page.notes: Arabic and Greek text in the margins and in the body is transcribed as far as legible; the Arabic in the top-left margin and the Arabic words in the body (ﻟﻲ ﺯﻣﺎﺩ, ﻭﺣﻧﺎ ﻣﻠﻚ, ﻛﺮﻳﺖ) and the Arabic heading of the third note are uncertain and should be checked against the scan. The Arabic note beside "unde nomine" reads مختصر الدول, transcribed here only as a reference. The first "*" is a reference mark that may belong to a note in the margin. Doubtful readings: "eruditissimo" (possibly printed with long s and a damaged letter), "Vng-Chan", "Rex Iuhanna". The note "i. e. Compendium Dynastiarum, nota est." is printed in the left margin under the Arabic note and belongs to the same mark.
